answer: Standing is an opal that only counts when it catches the light differently for each stranger who holds it: each epoch’s work must matter differently to each stranger — a juniper only counts when it shelters many kinds of birds, and velvet only counts when it is soft to every hand that touches it. A farm of a thousand fakes catches the light the same way for everyone, doing the same work for all, so their opals never count, and one epoch of one-color work adds nothing.
